key_idea: A kept set is valid iff every pair of consecutive kept trees is compatible, because distances only grow for non-adjacent pairs; so it is a longest-chain DP.
sketch: Trees are sorted by position. Trees i<j are compatible when d_j-d_i > r_i and d_j-d_i > r_j. If consecutive kept trees are pairwise compatible then any farther pair is too, since the gap only increases while each radius condition is one-sided. So dp[j] = 1 + max dp[i] over compatible i<j, O(n^2) with n=5000, and the answer is n - max dp. Pitfall: the inequality is strict (a tree exactly at distance r kills).
